stories.headline: GitHub sets an October deadline for several Copilot models

image.alt: Model lifecycle migration illustration showing current Copilot model inventory, affected workflows, replacement-model evaluation, policy updates, testing, and migration before the October 19, 2026 deadline.

stories.summary: GitHub says selected models will be removed from Copilot experiences on October 19, creating a concrete migration deadline for teams that depend on model-specific behavior in chat, edits, agent mode, or completions.

stories.headline: Copilot code review adds clearer progress and smarter suggestion handling

image.alt: Governed AI code-review illustration showing pull request intake, AI suggestions, human and automated checks, merge gates, suggestion states, policy controls, and full review traceability.

stories.summary: GitHub updated Copilot code review with clearer visibility into review progress, more intelligent auto-resolution of suggestions, and generated commit messages when developers accept batches of proposed changes.
stories.why_it_matters: AI-assisted review is moving from isolated comments toward a more stateful review workflow. Better progress visibility and suggestion lifecycle handling can reduce review friction, but teams still need controls for what gets accepted and how changes are verified.

stories.headline: IBM finds a gap between AI supervision needs and employee priorities

image.alt: Human-judgment control-layer illustration showing AI output, validation and assessment, risk-based decisions, override and correction, evidence tracing, uncertainty indicators, and accountability.

stories.summary: IBM reports that 71% of surveyed CHROs identify the ability to supervise, validate, and override AI outputs as a critical workforce skill, while only 29% of employees rank judgment as important, alongside concerns about skills erosion.
stories.why_it_matters: Organizations may be scaling AI faster than they are building the human judgment needed to use it responsibly. The practical challenge is to make verification, escalation, and override behavior part of everyday work rather than abstract AI training.

source.title: New IBM CHRO Study: AI Puts Critical Thinking at the Center of Workforce Priorities

stories.selection_rationale: Current workforce research directly relevant to human oversight and verification of AI outputs.

what_to_do_now.label: Teach verification, not just prompting
what_to_do_now.rationale: Add exercises that require employees to challenge AI outputs, validate evidence, recognize uncertainty, and know when to override or escalate.

stories.headline: AWS packages domain methodology into 38 open-source Agent Skills

image.alt: Reusable Agent Skills illustration showing expert methodology captured as a structured Skill, stored in a governed library, invoked by an agent, and validated against domain-specific checks.

stories.summary: AWS describes a collection of 38 open-source Agent Skills across 11 healthcare and life-sciences domains, using structured skill files to give agents reusable domain methods and reporting a 410-prompt evaluation with strong win rates.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a concrete example of the Agent Skills pattern moving beyond generic productivity tasks. Reusable skill packages can encode domain methods, checks, and procedures so an agent does not have to rediscover expert practice from scratch on every request.

stories.headline: AWS redesigns AgentCore runtime for elastic scale and faster agent starts

image.alt: Production agent runtime illustration showing variable demand, elastic managed runtime capacity, agent execution with models and tools, monitoring and telemetry, service outcomes, and failure handling.

stories.summary: AWS details changes to the AgentCore managed runtime aimed at elastic scaling, optimized resource use, and consistently faster starts for deployed agents, addressing infrastructure behavior that becomes visible once agents move into production workloads.
stories.why_it_matters: For non-technical leaders, agent reliability depends on the runtime as much as on the model. Slow starts, scaling limits, and operational friction can determine whether an agent feels dependable enough to become part of a business process.
